about: Characters beyond the poet and the three speakers of Part 3. `named`: couplets that name the figure, with the word they use, in its dictionary form; a `why` and `basis` (inferred) mark a name that rests on parimēlaḻagar’s reading. `involved`: couplets whose setting, in parimēlaḻagar’s note on who speaks and to whom, includes someone the couplet never names. `addressedBy`: speakers (he, she or maid) who talk to them, and where. export-fork.ts turns each into a Character node and its links, and places it in the lotus beside its couplets.

characters.label: God
characters.desc: The subject of the first chapter, praised in each couplet by a different name: the First, the one of pure knowledge, the one without likes or dislikes, the one beyond compare.

characters.label: Indra
characters.desc: Named in Kural 25 as “the lord of those in the wide sky”, witness enough to the power of one who has quenched the desires of the five senses.

characters.label: Tirumal
characters.desc: Named in Kural 610 as “the one who measured with his feet”: Tirumal, who took the worlds in three strides. A king who never slackens gains all that he strode across.

characters.label: Lakshmi
characters.desc: Fortune as a goddess. She lives with the generous host and the hard worker, and hands the envious over to her elder sister.

named.why: Named as திரு, fortune, which parimēlaḻagar reads as the goddess.
Named as திரு, fortune, which parimēlaḻagar reads as the goddess.

characters.label: Mūdēvi
characters.role: Goddess of misfortune, Lakshmi’s elder sister
characters.desc: Misfortune as a goddess. She lives in sloth, and gambling is called by her name.

characters.label: Death
characters.desc: Death as a god who takes lives. He cannot reach one who never kills, and in Part 3 her look is likened to him.

characters.label: Kāmaṉ
characters.desc: Named once, in Kural 1197. She asks whether the god of desire, who torments only one of the two lovers, cannot see her pain.

characters.label: Aṇaṅgu
characters.desc: A divine woman who takes life through desire, in parimēlaḻagar’s words. He wonders if she is one when he first sees her, and the embrace of false women is called one.

characters.label: Deities
characters.desc: The deities together, named in passing: even their worship fails without rain, and one who lives well on earth is placed among them.

characters.label: The Ancestors
characters.desc: Named in Kural 43, first of the five a householder keeps: the ancestors, the deities, guests, kin and himself.

characters.label: His Friend
characters.desc: His friend in Part 3, known from parimēlaḻagar’s notes. He chides the man for his love, arranges their meeting, and later carries his message. He never speaks a couplet.

addressedBy.why: He speaks to his friend in Kurals 1103, 1113 and 1201, in parimēlaḻagar’s notes.

involved.why: Said to his friend, who told him that one fit for the highest joy shouldn’t be so taken with this small one.
Said at the end of the meeting his friend arranged.
He tells his friend, who is bringing them together, what she is like.
Said as he goes to her, at the meeting his friend arranged.
Said to his friend, who went to her as his messenger.

characters.label: The Foster-Mother
characters.desc: The woman’s foster-mother in Part 3, known from parimēlaḻagar’s note on Kural 1140.

involved.why: Her friend has told the foster-mother of the love, and then teased her about it. Cross with her friend, she says this to herself.

characters.label: The Other Women
characters.desc: The courtesans he goes to in Part 3, known from parimēlaḻagar’s notes on the couplets where she sulks when he comes back.

involved.why: He has come back from other women, and she gave in. Asked by her friend why she didn’t sulk, she answers.
He has come back from other women. Sulking, she says this to him.
The same scene. In parimēlaḻagar’s reading, “those who sulk” are the other women, now cross with him.
In parimēlaḻagar’s reading, the “womanly ones” whose eyes all feast on him are the courtesans.

characters.label: The Town
characters.desc: The people of her town in Part 3, whose gossip about the lovers she fears and, at times, welcomes.
